editorial:
You follow Forrest, a kind man with a low IQ who keeps showing up at huge moments in history. He runs, fights, plays football, and even starts a shrimp business, all while chasing Jenny, the woman he has loved since childhood. The story feels warm, funny, and surprisingly sad as Forrest stays honest and calm while the world around him keeps changing. You will feel like you are sitting beside him on a park bench as he tells you his whole life story.

The acting is the big draw, especially Tom Hanks making Forrest feel real without turning him into a joke. The music, famous scenes, and mix of humor and heart keep you watching, though some moments feel a little too neat or old-fashioned. If you want a feel-good classic with tears and laughs, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Forrest learns Jenny is sick and they finally marry. After Jenny dies, Forrest raises their son and takes him to school on his first day. The twist is that Forrest never needed to be smart to live a full life; his simple kindness and steady love mattered most. He sits at the bus stop again, watching his son head off, and you see that his story continues through the next generation.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional stories, classic movies, and characters you root for.
